**BAAI/Emu3.5-Image** is an open-source, 34-billion-parameter image generation model from Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, while **Nano Banana 2** is Google DeepMind's closed-source commercial image model (officially *Gemini 3.1 Flash Image*), launched on February 26, 2026. The two represent very different philosophies: one is a freely accessible research model, the other is a production-grade commercial product optimized for speed and ecosystem integration.

## Origins and Architecture

BAAI/Emu3.5-Image is the image-specialized variant of the broader Emu3.5 multimodal world model. The full Emu3.5 was pre-trained end-to-end on over **10 trillion interleaved vision-language tokens**, primarily sourced from sequential internet video frames and transcripts. It uses a standard decoder-only transformer architecture and a unified next-token prediction objective, meaning it treats images just like text: as sequences of discrete tokens. The Emu3.5-Image variant strips away general-purpose multimodal tasks and focuses entirely on text-to-image (T2I) and any-to-image (X2I) synthesis for maximum performance on generation tasks.[1][2]

Nano Banana 2, on the other hand, is built on the Gemini 3.1 Flash architecture. It is Google's third image model in the "Nano Banana" family, following the original Nano Banana (August 2025) and Nano Banana Pro (November 2025). Google designed it to combine *Pro-level* visual quality with *Flash-level* speed and pricing, aiming to be their default image generation model across most products.[3][4][5]

## Speed and Inference

One of the biggest practical differences is inference speed. Nano Banana 2 generates images in **3–5 seconds** for standard resolutions, with real-world 4K outputs completing in 8–15 seconds. This speed is native to its Flash-tier architecture.[6]

Emu3.5-Image, in its base form, relies on token-by-token autoregressive decoding, which means each image can take **several minutes** to generate. However, BAAI has developed and is rolling out **DiDA (Discrete Diffusion Adaptation)**, which converts sequential decoding into bidirectional parallel prediction and achieves approximately **20× speedup** without sacrificing quality. DiDA-accelerated weights were still being finalized as of the model's public release, but once available, the gap in speed narrows dramatically.[2][1]

## Image Quality and Benchmarks

### Generation Benchmarks

| Dimension | BAAI/Emu3.5-Image | Nano Banana 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Text-rich image generation (LeX-Bench, LongText-Bench) | State-of-the-art, outperforms Nano Banana (v1) [7] | Strong, but trails on text-heavy benchmarks [8] |
| LM Arena Elo | Not officially ranked | 1,360 (top tier) [6] |
| Interleaved vision-language generation | Superior (65.5% world exploration win rate vs. Nano Banana v1) [7] | Not applicable (image-only model) |
| Max output resolution | 1024×1024 native (DiDA) | Up to **4K (4096×4096)** [6] |
| Subject consistency | Not a documented feature | Up to **5 characters + 14 objects** [9] |
| Aspect ratios | Flexible (native training) | 14 options including ultra-wide 8:1 and 1:8 [10] |
| Web search grounding | ✗ | ✓ via `enable_web_search` [10] |
| Multilingual text in images | English + Chinese + math formulas [7] | Multilingual translation within images [11] |
| Open source | ✅ Fully open weights | ❌ Closed commercial API |

It's important to note that the Emu3.5 paper's direct comparisons were made against the **original Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image)**, not Nano Banana 2. Nano Banana 2 launched in February 2026, after Emu3.5's release, and brings meaningful quality improvements over its predecessor. Emu3.5-Image's benchmarks show it **matches or slightly edges out** Nano Banana v1 on image generation/editing tasks and clearly outperforms it on interleaved and text-rich tasks. How it stacks up directly against Nano Banana 2 on pure image quality is not yet fully benchmarked in peer-reviewed literature.[8][12][3]

## Access, Pricing, and Ecosystem

Nano Banana 2 costs **$0.039 per image** at standard resolution and is tightly integrated into Google products including the Gemini app, Google Search, and Google Ads. All outputs carry **SynthID digital watermarking** and will gain C2PA Content Credentials. It supports up to 4 images per batch request.[11][4][10]

Emu3.5-Image is freely available on Hugging Face under BAAI's open-source license. You can run it locally or through platforms like Replicate, which hosts it at **34 billion parameters**. The cost is essentially compute cost rather than per-image API pricing, making it attractive for high-volume or research use cases where API bills would otherwise be prohibitive.[13][14]

## Unique Strengths of Each Model

Emu3.5-Image excels in **text-rich image generation** — producing images that contain accurate, legible text including complex mathematical formulas, long paragraphs, and multilingual content. This is a well-known weakness for many diffusion-based models. Its training on 10+ trillion tokens of video data also gives it a nuanced understanding of physical causality and scene coherence that manifests in generation quality.[7][13]

Nano Banana 2's standout features are its **production readiness** and **subject consistency**. Being able to lock the appearance of up to five characters and fourteen objects across a multi-image workflow  is extremely valuable for storyboarding, advertising, and brand content. Its integration with real-time web search grounding also lets it render specific real-world subjects — logos, landmarks, product designs — more accurately than models trained on static datasets alone.[9][11]

## Which Should You Choose?

If you need a **free, locally runnable model** with exceptional text-in-image capability, research transparency, and strong multimodal generation, BAAI/Emu3.5-Image is the clear choice. If you need **fast, scalable, commercially licensed image generation** with 4K output, subject consistency, and deep Google ecosystem integration — and you're comfortable with API pricing — Nano Banana 2 is the more practical and polished tool. The two models aren't so much direct competitors as they are solutions optimized for very different users: Emu3.5-Image for open-source researchers and developers, and Nano Banana 2 for production applications and business workflows.[5][1][13][11]
